analysis.title: US Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (October 30, 2026)
key_insights: Futures are weaker after MegaCap Tech earnings disappointed: AMZN -7.3% and INTC -25.7% pre-market, pulling Semis (SOXX -6%) and Memory (DRAM -5.6%) lower. JPM expects the equity rotation to continue but says the broad indices will reflect Tech's downside.
Pre-market the SPX is -1.0%, NDX -2.3% and RTY -0.5%. WTI is +202bps at $104.06, the 10Y is at 4.933% and VIX is at 18.38. Gold is -73bps at $3,992 and silver -268bps at $50.75.

Q3 GDP printed +3.4%. Headline PCE rose from 3.4% to 3.6% YoY and Core PCE from 3.0% to 3.1%. The Q3 GDP price index came in at 2.3% against 3.2% expected, and Core PCE QoQ fell from 3.3% to 2.5%. The yield curve bull steepened, and JPM says this backdrop stays supportive of the ex-AI trade.

GOOG earnings showed residual fragility in the AI theme. The market is expressing a Broadening vs. AI view, and JPM calls the AI trade crowded with exceptionally high sentiment bars to clear even after hyperscaler and Memory earnings, positive reception of S-1 filings and some positioning reset. Midway through earnings season it is open whether Tech or non-Tech leads.

Chase spending data shows total October spending up about 5.8% Y/Y MTD through Oct 21, slower than September's 6.8%. Discretionary growth slowed to 5.4% from 6.9% while non-discretionary growth edged up to 6.7% from 6.6%.

Energy headlines: Russia extends its diesel export ban to year-end, XOM and CVX executives cancelled a UAE oil show trip on security concerns, Kpler data cited on X puts Strait of Hormuz exports below 11mm bpd on a 7-day average against 20.5mm pre-war, and Yemeni forces are said to be targeting Aramco. Iran restated its 7 conditions for ending the war, and Karl Rove sees Trump attacking Iran after the midterms.

Midterms: the Kansas Senate race is tightening, Alaska and Ohio moved toward GOP candidates and Maine, Michigan and Texas toward Democrats. A NY Times poll has South Carolina tied while prediction markets give the GOP candidate a 72% chance.

TMT desk (Heavey): the GOOGL sell-off is driving rotation within hyperscalers, with META the clear beneficiary as it works back toward its $625 equity offering price. AMZN is selling off because the Azure beat raised the AWS bar, with some fear of an equity raise. MSFT is not trading better after a big Azure beat, and semicap names are outperforming on a better KLAC print.

TMT desk on SOXX weakness: it cites MRVL being hit on a potential deal with LITE, Samsung earnings (the desk sees the only real issue as lack of capital return) and capex-peaking worries. The desk pushes back on capex peaking, saying ORCL has to tell investors it is done raising capital and MSFT's lower capex was timing. Desk flows are elevated and risk off, security software is for sale after FTNT, and NOW stays near lows.

Consumer desk (Murphy): Discretionary is outperforming and the fundamental backdrop is constructive after healthy prints (CMG, CROX, NCLH, hotels). Flows still look like squeeze and hedge fund pain, not a wholesale re-risk. Long-only supply persists in RSI, HSY, USFD, SVV, SMPL, HD and NCLH, and most large upside movers were crowded shorts. Strength in OLLI, BURL, CAVA and TPR is read as positioning unwind after bearish data reads proved wrong.

Utilities desk (Henrici): net buying in utilities was +1.5z yesterday, the 92nd percentile for single-day net buying over the past year. Two weeks of net buying brought MTD net flows to flat, and XLU took about $1bn of net inflows over the past month on net assets just above $20bn.

Fins desk (O'Dwyer): more tech investors are looking to become defensive, which fits his card network 'Indian summer' view and NDAQ's outperformance. He lists fintech and info services names of interest if the bid from tech investors continues.

Positioning Intelligence (Nikos): retail investors poured record amounts into leveraged ETFs over the past couple of weeks, supporting a bottoming in AI-related stocks, and JPM sees room for the retail impulse to grow into year-end, particularly via options. QQQ short interest is at its highest since 2023, and tech buybacks have been resilient YTD despite higher capex.

Nikos on futures and other flows: momentum investors unwound shorts in government bond futures and longs in equity futures. Shorts in 10y OATs vs Bunds and the euro, and longs in crude oil and TTF futures, remain elevated. Retail inflows into Brazil reversed modestly after the election while institutions cut exposure. Short interest support for bitcoin vs. gold via IBIT vs GLD has faded, though other metrics still favor bitcoin.

JPM remains Tactically Bullish. SPX is down 2.4% over two weeks and -36bp MTD, with 8 of 11 sectors positive. The basis is trend-or-better growth (Flash PMIs imply about 5% annualized real growth) and earnings tracking pre-season forecasts, but JPM says a full positioning washout has not occurred even with sentiment in the Fear region.

Last week the Recession L/S and Stagflation L/S baskets both outperformed, returning 3.4% and 1.5%. Trump said he is nearing a decision on Iran between negotiation and continued attacks while a third aircraft carrier approaches. JPM expects a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy if he returns to negotiations. Iran says new bombing would bring strikes on the region including Israel and the UAE.
The updated Monetization Menu says the prior menu still aligns with the view and would consider adding hedges via longs in oil and Energy equities plus long vol.

sector_views.rationale: The Oct 19 Monetization Menu, which JPM says still aligns with its view, retains a preference for Tech via pairs trades and derivatives. Near-term the desk sees AI fragility and risk-off flows.
Constructive in the Oct 19 menu on consumer resilience and limited direct exposure to AI concerns.
Constructive in the Oct 19 menu for the same reasons as Financials. The consumer desk sees squeeze-driven moves, not a broad rotation.

earnings_insights: AMZN fell 7.3% pre-market and INTC 25.7% pre-market after their reports, per the morning update. No EPS figures are given.

Per the TMT desk, MSFT posted a big Azure beat in its July-quarter print yet is not trading better. The Azure beat raised the bar for AWS at AMZN. KLAC delivered a better print and semicap names are outperforming.
GOOG earnings 'highlighted the residual fragility of the AI theme' per JPM. The news links cite Google erasing a record $500 billion in market value.
Consumer prints (CMG, CROX, NCLH, hotels) were solid, but the desk reads upside in crowded shorts (NCLH, CROX, BOOT, CVNA, CMG) as a squeeze.
Pre-earnings-season forecast, per the Oct 26 view: about 13% revenue growth, about 30% EPS growth and about 15% margins. About a quarter of the SPX had reported with no dips to that forecast.
Reporting today before the open: ABBV, CBOE, CL, CVX, EXC, GD, LYB, REGN, XOM and others. A news link says Big Oil earnings are set to surge.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Beat expectations per the CNBC link and supports the ex-AI trade per JPM.
Inflation re-accelerated, though the quarterly price components were softer.
Below expectations, which helped the yield curve bull steepen.
Expected level that the 2.3% print undershot.
Quarterly core inflation slowed, contributing to the bull steepening.
Spending growth decelerated month over month, driven by discretionary categories.

crypto_views: Bitcoin has less support vs. gold from the previously elevated short interest in IBIT vs. GLD, but other metrics continue to favor bitcoin over gold.
Retail investors are pouring record amounts into leveraged equity ETFs, which JPM links to a bottoming in AI-related stocks.

risk_factors: Iran escalation if Trump chooses continued attacks over negotiation, with Iran threatening the region including Israel and the UAE.
AI monetization fears and a crowded AI trade with very high sentiment bars, plus possible equity raises at AMZN and ORCL.
Capex-peaking worries and further hyperscaler and semiconductor earnings disappointments.
No complete positioning washout yet despite Fear-level sentiment.
Oil supply disruption: Hormuz exports below 11mm bpd, Russian diesel export ban, Yemeni attacks targeting Aramco.
Event risk from the Nov 1 trade truce expiry, the Nov 3 midterms and the Dec 11 government funding deadline.
vol_and_positioning: Desk flows are elevated and risk off. Security software is for sale and GOOGL supply is relentless. Enterprise SaaS shows some covering but NOW is near lows.
QQQ short interest rose to its highest level since 2023, which JPM says leaves a short base for institutions to cover.
Momentum investors unwound shorts in government bond futures and longs in equity futures. Shorts in 10y OATs vs Bunds and the euro remain elevated, as do longs in crude oil and TTF futures.
Utilities saw +1.5z net buying (92nd percentile over the past year) and about $1bn of XLU inflows over the past month.
Consumer long-only supply continues while upside concentrates in crowded shorts, so the desk calls it squeeze and selective re-engagement.
JPM says a complete positioning washout has not occurred even though sentiment is firmly in the Fear region. The AI trade remains crowded.
Hedge idea in the Monetization Menu: longs in oil and Energy equities plus long vol.
geopolitical: Russia extends its diesel export ban to year-end.

Karl Rove sees Trump attacking Iran after the midterms (The Hill). Trump says he is nearing a decision between negotiation and continued attacks on Iran as a third aircraft carrier nears the region, with no strikes on Sunday while the US moves personnel out of the region.
Iran says any new bombing would result in it targeting the region, including Israel and the UAE, and reiterates 7 conditions for progress on ending the war.
Kpler data cited on X points to Strait of Hormuz exports below 11mm bpd on a 7-day average vs. 20.5mm pre-war.
The Yemeni army is said to be targeting Aramco in missile attacks. CVX and XOM executives cancelled a trip to the UAE oil show on security concerns.
The one-year trade truce between Trump and Xi expires Nov 1, and the report cites NBC saying the US and China agreed to extend it through January 20, 2027.
DOJ says ATF and DEA agents will serve as poll monitors but none from FBI or ICE ahead of the Nov 3 midterms.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI theme has climbed the wall of worry with hyperscaler and Memory earnings, a positive reception to S-1 filings, some positioning reset and record retail flows into leveraged ETFs. The TMT desk argues capex is not peaking and tech buybacks have been resilient.
tension_points.bear_case: GOOG earnings showed residual fragility, AMZN and INTC fell sharply pre-market, the trade is crowded with exceptionally high sentiment bars to clear, and desk flows are elevated and risk off. The macro backdrop favors the ex-AI trade.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The TMT desk says capex-peaking worries fade only if ORCL tells investors it is done raising capital. A fresh equity raise at AMZN or ORCL would undercut the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: An economy growing at or above trend GDP and positive earnings growth produce a bull market. Earnings are tracking the pre-season forecast, and a return to negotiations with Iran would spark a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy.
tension_points.bear_case: A complete positioning washout has not occurred, and Trump may continue attacks on Iran, which has said new bombing would bring strikes on the region including Israel and the UAE.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Trump choosing continued attacks over negotiation and Iran retaliating against the region, including Israel and the UAE.

tension_points.bull_case: Consumer spending is healthy across a solid slate of prints, lower rates and oil help the setup, and Discretionary is outperforming.
tension_points.bear_case: Flows look like squeeze and hedge fund pain, long-only selling persists and upside is concentrated in heavily shorted names.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of long-only dollars rotating into the Consumer space, which the desk says it is not yet seeing.

theme_stances.key_argument: The macro environment remains supportive of the ex-AI trade after the GDP and PCE prints.
theme_stances.evidence: remains supportive of the ex-AI trade

theme_stances.key_argument: Trend-or-better growth and earnings growth produce a bull market, so a refocus on fundamentals over AI fears should support stocks.
A return to negotiations would bring a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy, while continued attacks remain the key risk.
